correctness.rationale: For A=z−α, B=z−β and D=p′(z)(z−w)−p(z), the numerators of F−α and F−β over D are −A²(w−β) and −B²(w−α). Their ratio gives a²/b directly, including for arbitrary distinct roots. Composition gives second coordinates b²/a and b³/a² and ratio powers q=3 and 4. Both variants have a_k=a_0 r_0^N and b_k=b_0 r_0^(−δN), N=(q^k−1)/(q−1), δ=q−2. Off |r|=1, neither a full collision (r=1) nor the cyclic intermediate collision (r²=1) can occur; precisely a=1 or b=1 at some iterate signals a pole. The two stated initial pairs each have the claimed first-sweep pole and avoid all future poles in the opposite method, by their explicit magnitudes. The inverse cross-ratio formula bounds the slower coordinate error above and below by constants times exp(−N|log|r_0||). On |r|=1 both transformed moduli stay fixed and cannot approach either root. For m≥2 a primitive root of order N_m gives return at m and no earlier return since 0<N_j<N_m for j<m. The ratio never becomes ±1 as its order is N_m>2 and coprime to q; |a|=|b|=2 avoids affine infinity. In local logarithmic coordinates the derivative of the return is the mth power of the exponent matrix, hence has multipliers 1 and q^m; an open set cannot be attracted since any nearby orbit off the unit-modulus separator either leaves the domain or tends to a root permutation.
residual_risks: No classification of singular projective continuations or higher-degree or rounded iterates. Openness off the separator uses the explicit uniformly small/large tail on a neighborhood, leaving only finitely many pole conditions there.

evidence: In root coordinates a root-fixing Möbius map multiplies a,b by the same scalar, so any admissible generic pair may be normalized to ab=1, the symmetric subfamily. The n=2 formula cubes its first cross-ratio coordinate; undoing the scaling gives the generic Jacobi component a²/b.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This also makes it easy to obtain the sequential component formula by substitution. The distinct claim analyzed here is not the bare rational update: it controls the sequential orbit and its exclusion sets in affine coordinates, evaluates its sharp asymptotic error and proves existence and instability for every regular least period, in direct comparison to the parallel rule.

value.rationale: Degree two is the first nontrivial instance of a standard simultaneous root finder and a natural exact baseline when larger degrees exhibit attracting failures. A common basin rule does not mean identical exceptional starts or speed. Exact pole distinctions, the sharp fourth-power versus third-power error scale, and abundant nonattracting cycles describe concrete ways the update order matters beyond the elementary update identity.
residual_risks: This exact baseline is not a floating-point guarantee or a predictor of higher-degree basin topology.
